text:
maya: FYI support escalation from Acme — they're seeing a jump in 503s and timeouts to our hosted inference API after the 02:00 deploy. customer-impacting, high volume. link to dashboard: https://dash.redwood.example/org/acme/requests

jon: can you paste a sample request id and any error payloads? do we know which model/route? :eyes:

maya: sample request ids: req_0a9f2c, req_0a9f2d. route: /v1/generate (model: open-lm-v2-13b; variant: quantized). snippet from customer logs: ```{"request_id":"req_0a9f2c","status":503,"error":"gateway timeout","latency_ms":12045}```

kevin: looks like the canary we pushed included the sticky-token-propagation flag enabled. that's the only change touching headers in this deploy. config diff: ```- header_propagation: false\n+ header_propagation: token-forwarding-v2```

sriram: if token propagation changed, backend auth servers might be rejecting or slowing requests leading to gateway timeouts. can we confirm auth service 5xx around same window?

deploy-bot: Deploy 2026-03-17T02:00 UTC by kevin completed. Canary 10% -> 25% traffic. Rollout ID: r-20260317-02-canary-7

maya: customer reports spike started ~02:12 UTC which aligns with canary increase. they're seeing ~15% request failures overall and timeouts for long-tail latencies. billing-bot flagged anomaly: increased retries from Acme causing billing spike.

alex-pm: priority = P1 for Acme (enterprise). we need a mitigation plan and ETA to either rollback or patch.

jon: quick repro steps for eng-runtime: curl to reproduce (from inside prod cluster to mimic routing): ```curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"prompt":"hi","max_tokens":10}' https://api.redwood.internal/v1/generate?model=open-lm-v2-13b``` observed response: hangs ~12s then 503.

kevin: repro locally against canary nodes shows increased auth handshake latency. stacktrace excerpt from runtime logs: ```2026-03-17T02:11:58Z ERROR auth-client/req_0a9f2c timeout waiting for token introspection (upstream 504) at auth-client.go:218```

sriram: immediate mitigations: 1) scale auth client concurrency down to avoid cascades? (risky) 2) pin traffic away from canary (recommended) 3) rollback config change entirely.

kevin: agree. can we gate rollforward and do traffic shift to 0% for rollout r-20260317-02-canary-7?

deploy-bot: Action: shift-traffic r-20260317-02-canary-7 -> 0% requested by jon. Running...

deploy-bot: Action completed. Canary r-20260317-02-canary-7 traffic at 0%. Default stable reverted to previous model/variant.

jon: confirm metrics please. maya can you ask Acme to retry? I'll keep watch on infra dashboards.

maya: Acme says failures dropped to ~0.8% within 2 minutes after traffic shift. they're happy to test.

kevin: I'll open a PR to revert header_propagation change and add an integration test around token-forwarding with auth-introspection timeouts. also flagging that rollout automation shouldn't increase canary weight >10% until 15m observation.

alex-pm: good. capture postmortem and follow-up actions: add canary guardrails, add circuit breaker around auth-introspection, update billing alert thresholds for retry storms.

sriram: logging note: collect full auth trace for req_0a9f2c/req_0a9f2d and put into incident artifact bucket. I'll push retention of 7 days for these spans.

maya: adding customer follow-up: proposed fix + rollback accepted. will send message to Acme CS and request confirm once they finish smoke tests. :thumbsup:

jon: thanks everyone. leaving oncall to monitor for 20m and then handoff. :white_check_mark:
